title: Thyroid hormone treatment and breast cancer risk in women: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies
authors: Kopanos S, Feldkamp JD, Tyssen J, Li X, Sundquist K, Pape-Köhler C, et al.
population: Observational studies of adult women receiving thyroid hormone against non-users, searched January 1976 to February 2025; primary analysis of 4 studies with 221,254 treated women and 4,385,666 controls: adjusted odds ratios from 3 case-control studies (Kapdi, Shapiro, Wu) and a crude odds ratio calculated from author-provided counts of the Swedish register cohort of Wändell 2020 (4,271,551 people), whose authors Wändell, Li and Sundquist co-authored this meta-analysis
funder: This research received no external funding.
authorConflicts: All authors declare that they have no conflicts of interest related to this work.
result: Pooled odds ratio for breast cancer with thyroid hormone treatment 1.43 (95% CI 0.90 to 2.28; I2 94.3%) in the abstract and 1.45 (0.93 to 2.27) in the results text; 95% prediction interval 0.43 to 4.92; without the Wändell cohort 1.40 (0.59 to 3.28). Certainty of evidence low because of heterogeneity, inconsistency and imprecision. The authors describe the result as a possible, hypothesis-generating signal with residual confounding.
